reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (E-03) because a change to the billing import validation rules around that time is the best-supported locus of systematic bill-calculation errors, consistent with tariff changes being ruled out (E-04) and with the majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills being billed from ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimates (E-05), i.e. the defect affects both read paths, not just estimate substitution. This is a bill-correctness problem in the billing-import step, not a ticket-handling capacity shortfall, since dispute response times remain inside the 3.0-day SLA (E-02).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (E-03) because billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 history without unit scaling (E-13), causing valid high-consumption AMI reads to be wrongly rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and estimate-substituted, which accounts for 95.5% of the ESTIMATED-read dispute share (E-12). This mechanism explains the minority (41%, 1240/3025) of disputed bills billed on estimates, while the majority (59%, 1785/3025) ACTUAL-read disputed bills remain causally unexplained by it (E-05).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
